findings.premise: Non-goal 3 ("Add daemon/indexer dependencies to the reusable package") is semantically consistent with, not contradicted by, constraint k1's requirement of "independent build/test consumption" with "insrc daemon is an adapter host" — i.e. the reusable module must build/test without the daemon while the daemon only adapts to it.
findings.evidence: DEF.md:74 states non-goal 3: "Add daemon/indexer dependencies to the reusable package. — Independent external applications must consume the feature without insrc startup." DEF.md:85 states k1: "Deliver one self-contained Node/TypeScript module with embedded and standalone IPC modes, public versioned interfaces, injected host dependencies and independent build/test consumption; insrc daemon is an adapter host." The non-goal's rationale (consume without insrc startup) and k1's requirements (independent build/test consumption, daemon as adapter host, injected host dependencies) both point the same direction: the reusable module must not depend on daemon/indexer internals, and the daemon only adapts to the module rather than the module depending on it. No wording in either anchor contradicts the other.

body.title: Share project memory across agents and applications
body.problem: Project knowledge acquired in a coding conversation does not reliably survive a switch of agent, session or application. Developers repeat instructions, decisions and handoff context; verbose retained transcripts obscure the current rule, while similar or conflicting statements accumulate without clear scope, provenance or lifecycle. Acknowledged context can be lost after a crash, stale context can override corrections or deletions, and applications outside the existing background service cannot depend on a common memory capability without inheriting unrelated runtime dependencies.

nonGoals.text: Replace static instruction-file generation, native agent session stores, code indexing or workflow approvals.
nonGoals.rationale: These remain authoritative in their existing domains; memory links to them and cannot manufacture permission.

nonGoals.text: Automatic cross-user synchronization, personal profiling, multimodal ingestion or unrestricted import of private histories.
nonGoals.rationale: Initial scope is explicit local project memory with privacy and project binding.

nonGoals.text: Add daemon/indexer dependencies to the reusable package.
nonGoals.rationale: Independent external applications must consume the feature without insrc startup.

assumptions.text: First delivery targets local single-user projects and supported coding agents; native capture capabilities differ by agent and must be qualified.
Provider and IPC implementations offer adapter candidates, not proof that they can be imported unchanged by an independent package.

constraints.text: Deliver one self-contained Node/TypeScript module with embedded and standalone IPC modes, public versioned interfaces, injected host dependencies and independent build/test consumption; insrc daemon is an adapter host.

Sessions only submit to a separate durable file queue; one context-builder worker owns every memory-store mutation, receipt and maintenance operation per configured directory. Acknowledge only after durable append; size rotates segments, never discards pending events.
Memory authority and vectors use a dedicated LanceDB directory separate from index storage. Replay is at least once with idempotent committed effects and no resurrection after forgetting.

Normalize, deduplicate and compress without losing scope, polarity, conditions, authority or provenance. Support expansion, supersession, conflict, expiry and deletion; similarity alone cannot establish equivalence.

Inject inference and local embedding interfaces; insrc adapters enforce existing role policy, serial model execution and cloud access only through installed CLI providers. No direct cloud REST from the core.

Host validates project/session identity and privacy eligibility before durable capture. insrc binds to registered repos; external applications supply explicit binding. Embedded/IPC parity includes lifecycle, readiness, ownership, errors, retries and operation barriers.

summary.prose: Deliver a reusable shared project memory feature that keeps concise, traceable and current context available across coding agents and applications. Applications can host it directly or connect to an independent local service with equivalent behavior. Accepted submissions survive restart, and corrections and forgetting remain effective across replay.

stories.title: Host memory inside an external application
stories.userValue: An application can use shared memory without adopting the insrc runtime.

acceptanceCriteria.given: an external application supplies project identity, providers, policy and isolated storage paths
acceptanceCriteria.when: it imports and opens the memory module
acceptanceCriteria.then: import has no side effects, readiness is explicit and the application can use the public memory service without starting insrc

acceptanceCriteria.given: two hosts target the same memory directory
acceptanceCriteria.when: the second tries to open a writer
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is refused; distinct directories operate independently and closing memory preserves host-owned provider resources

functionalRequirements.statement: An application can use shared memory without adopting the insrc runtime.

stories.title: Accept project memory durably and recover interrupted ingestion
stories.userValue: An accepted submission remains available after a crash.

acceptanceCriteria.given: eligible submissions arrive from concurrent sessions
acceptanceCriteria.when: the service acknowledges acceptance and then terminates unexpectedly
acceptanceCriteria.then: each accepted complete event is recoverable with stable identity and ordering; a retry cannot create duplicate logical events

acceptanceCriteria.given: pending events exhaust the configured disk budget
acceptanceCriteria.when: new submissions arrive or queue files reach their size threshold
acceptanceCriteria.then: files rotate safely, pending work is retained and admission applies visible backpressure; truncated tails and corruption yield explicit recovery outcomes

functionalRequirements.statement: An accepted submission remains available after a crash.

stories.title: Keep current memory and processing outcomes consistent through replay
stories.userValue: A correction or forgotten memory cannot be undone by a restart.

acceptanceCriteria.given: an event changes canonical memory and processing status
acceptanceCriteria.when: execution fails before or after the durable commit boundary
acceptanceCriteria.then: recovery exposes either the prior state or the complete committed result and retries do not repeat committed effects

acceptanceCriteria.given: an existing record is corrected, superseded, expired or forgotten
acceptanceCriteria.when: old events replay or concurrent clients submit stale revisions
acceptanceCriteria.then: revision and deletion boundaries hold, lineage remains inspectable as allowed by retention, and operation status distinguishes pending, committed, failed and cleanup-pending

acceptanceCriteria.given: memory and code indexes use separate directories
acceptanceCriteria.when: either subsystem is reset or rebuilt
acceptanceCriteria.then: the other subsystem and pending memory submissions remain intact

functionalRequirements.statement: A correction or forgotten memory cannot be undone by a restart.

stories.title: Normalize and compress shared context without losing meaning
stories.userValue: Repeated statements produce concise current memory with reliable scope.

acceptanceCriteria.given: equivalent directives and supporting evidence arrive from different agents
acceptanceCriteria.when: normalization processes them
acceptanceCriteria.then: one canonical instruction is active with deduplicated supporting evidence, while conditions, negation, scope, identifiers and source authority are preserved

acceptanceCriteria.given: a new statement expands, contradicts or explicitly overrides prior context
acceptanceCriteria.when: reconciliation runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: it distinguishes expansion, conflict and authorized supersession; unresolved ambiguity is visible and similarity alone cannot merge or override

acceptanceCriteria.given: inference fails or its proposed compression loses material meaning
acceptanceCriteria.when: the worker processes the event
acceptanceCriteria.then: it retries or exposes a qualified failure without activating the lossy result, and all model work respects provider policy

functionalRequirements.statement: Repeated statements produce concise current memory with reliable scope.

stories.title: Recall compact current context and explain its sources
stories.userValue: A new session receives relevant instructions and handoff context without replaying a verbose transcript.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a project has directives, handoff facts and bounded historical evidence
acceptanceCriteria.when: a client asks for context or searches for an exact identifier or paraphrase
acceptanceCriteria.then: results are scoped, compact and source-traceable; mandatory directives are not silently omitted and overflow or degraded retrieval is explicit

acceptanceCriteria.given: a correction or forget operation has committed
acceptanceCriteria.when: a reader requests context using an operation barrier or previously cached view
acceptanceCriteria.then: the result reflects the committed generation, excludes invalidated memory and does not persist read-side effects outside the command path

acceptanceCriteria.given: a user inspects an item
acceptanceCriteria.when: they request its provenance or correction status
acceptanceCriteria.then: source spans, lineage, authority, conflicts and actual operation state are visible without exposing prohibited source material

functionalRequirements.statement: A new session receives relevant instructions and handoff context without replaying a verbose transcript.

stories.title: Use the same memory feature through an independent local service
stories.userValue: Applications can connect to memory without embedding its execution or running insrc.

acceptanceCriteria.given: the insrc daemon is stopped
acceptanceCriteria.when: a standalone memory process starts and an external IPC client connects
acceptanceCriteria.then: capture, context/search, inspection, correction, forgetting and status behave equivalently to embedded mode

acceptanceCriteria.given: a connection drops after submission or protocol versions differ
acceptanceCriteria.when: the client reconnects and retries or sends an incompatible request
acceptanceCriteria.then: event identity and commit barriers are preserved, unsupported contracts fail explicitly, and endpoint access and request validation remain enforced

acceptanceCriteria.given: accepted work exists when shutdown or forced termination occurs
acceptanceCriteria.when: the service stops and restarts
acceptanceCriteria.then: readiness, drain and shutdown outcomes are explicit, resources release safely and accepted unfinished work remains recoverable

functionalRequirements.statement: Applications can connect to memory without embedding its execution or running insrc.

stories.title: Carry shared memory between insrc-managed agents
stories.userValue: Switching coding agents in insrc preserves project instructions and handoff context.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a registered project runs managed Claude, Codex, Vibe or Ollama sessions
acceptanceCriteria.when: a session submits eligible attributed context and another provider begins work
acceptanceCriteria.then: the shared instruction and compact handoff are delivered through the common feature without partitioning by agent identity or opening storage in clients

acceptanceCriteria.given: a temporary/private execution, ambiguous project or detached client is encountered
acceptanceCriteria.when: capture or delivery is attempted
acceptanceCriteria.then: privacy eligibility is enforced before durable persistence, missing binding is explicit and no hook reports acceptance or context delivery without evidence

acceptanceCriteria.given: the host is VS Code, JetBrains or CLI/MCP
acceptanceCriteria.when: it inspects or changes memory through its supported integration
acceptanceCriteria.then: payload meaning and operation states agree; the deprecated insrc-ide fork is excluded

functionalRequirements.statement: Switching coding agents in insrc preserves project instructions and handoff context.

stories.title: Share memory with independently running coding CLIs
stories.userValue: Native coding sessions can participate with truthful support and capture status.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a supported installed CLI version has qualified hook or MCP capabilities
acceptanceCriteria.when: an independent Claude, Codex or Vibe session starts, resumes, compacts, interrupts or completes
acceptanceCriteria.then: eligible deltas and context delivery use the qualified adapter, have stable source identities and do not duplicate managed capture

acceptanceCriteria.given: required hook support or ingress is unavailable
acceptanceCriteria.when: native integration attempts capture or mandatory context delivery
acceptanceCriteria.then: capability limitations and not-captured/not-delivered states are visible; any fallback is explicitly durable and does not claim universal automatic per-turn support

functionalRequirements.statement: Native coding sessions can participate with truthful support and capture status.

stories.title: Maintain and evaluate memory without weakening deletion or authority
stories.userValue: Memory stays correct and bounded as evidence ages and processing changes.

acceptanceCriteria.given: retention, expiry, migration, re-embedding or physical forgetting is requested
acceptanceCriteria.when: maintenance executes or restarts after interruption
acceptanceCriteria.then: the sole writer preserves receipts, replay and tombstone boundaries; logical deletion and physical purge are separately reported including backup limitations

acceptanceCriteria.given: candidate lessons or duplicate consolidation arise
acceptanceCriteria.when: maintenance proposes active memory
acceptanceCriteria.then: evidence remains source-qualified, uncertain lessons do not gain directive authority and meaningful qualifiers survive

acceptanceCriteria.given: the full feature is ready for release
acceptanceCriteria.when: the behavioral, crash and quality evaluation suites run
acceptanceCriteria.then: embedded/IPC parity, privacy, isolation, exact and semantic recall, false-merge resistance and compression fidelity have recorded evidence with unresolved limitations explicit

functionalRequirements.statement: Memory stays correct and bounded as evidence ages and processing changes.

requirements.statement: Project context is available across supported agents with current scoped instructions, compact handoffs and inspectable historical evidence.
Semantically equivalent statements share one canonical memory while distinct scope and unresolved conflicts remain explicit.
Durably accepted submissions survive interruption and can be retried without duplicate memory effects.
Users can inspect, correct, expand, supersede, expire and forget memory with visible asynchronous processing status.
External applications can use the complete memory feature embedded or through an independent local IPC service without the insrc daemon.
Privacy exclusions, project isolation and deletion boundaries hold across capture, retrieval, caches, replay and cleanup.
An application can use shared memory without adopting the insrc runtime.
An accepted submission remains available after a crash.
A correction or forgotten memory cannot be undone by a restart.
Repeated statements produce concise current memory with reliable scope.
A new session receives relevant instructions and handoff context without replaying a verbose transcript.
Applications can connect to memory without embedding its execution or running insrc.
Switching coding agents in insrc preserves project instructions and handoff context.
Native coding sessions can participate with truthful support and capture status.
Memory stays correct and bounded as evidence ages and processing changes.
